endorsements.quote: First, red teaming involves stress-testing AI systems by simulating challenging scenarios under experimental conditions through techniques such as jailbreaking, prompt injection and adversarial attacks.

UNDCS can also be improved by extensive testing with repeated sampling and adjudication through LLM-as-a-Judge loops to score and verify aggregate output validity across multiple runs, albeit with some limitations11.

unlisted_practices: Regulators should create a new category of regulation for unconfined non-deterministic clinical software (UNDCS) that is not tied to manufacturer-designated intended-use labels.
Regulations for UNDCS should set standards for inclusion of safeguards such as red teaming, guardrails, agent-agent moderation and confined retrieval-augmented generation.
Implement guardrails such as Llama Guard or Guardrails AI to filter inappropriate LLM output, co-implemented with defences against adversarial attacks.
Use confined retrieval-augmented generation to ground LLM responses in validated, trusted knowledge sources.
Use multi-agent systems with agent-agent moderation, augmented by RAG checkpoints and neuro-symbolic models reasoning from validated guidelines, to reduce errors and align outputs with intended use.

Build safeguards into direct-to-consumer generative AI that demonstrably restrict outputs to non-medical-device use cases unless formally evaluated in clinical trials and deployed with ongoing quality controls.
Regulators should set acceptable risk mitigation standards for all UNDCS, including non-clinical administrative tools used in healthcare.
Involve clinicians early in red teaming and technical evaluation of generative AI.
Regulators should adopt agile, forward-looking frameworks that keep pace with generative AI and hold manufacturers accountable for the software they monetise.
